provenance.tool: property test; tests/reference/derive_cashflows.py (Python 3.13 standard library: fractions, decimal)
provenance.steps: Fixture: seven FIXED loans in EUR and USD with penalty NONE; market_rates.csv holds one refinancing series per currency at the as-of date 2024-01-31 (0.03 EUR, 0.04 USD) and at 2023-12-31, which must not be used; PM1 at fixed parameters c_min 0.02, c_max 0.30, k 100, x0 0.01, a_ramp 12 months, twelve seasonal factors with mean 1, b 0, margin 0.005 and lag 1 (M4). The curve is held from the as-of date, so with a one-month lag every projected month reads it. views: loan B1 (annuity, 10,000 at 4.5%, four months to 2024-05-31, originated 2023-06-15): I = 0.045 - (0.03 + 0.005) = 0.01 = x0, logistic = 1/2 and CPR = 0.16 x Ramp(age) x Season(month), age 7 to 10 months: 0.16 x 7/12 x 0.9 = 0.084, 0.16 x 8/12 x 1.0, 0.16 x 9/12 x 1.1 = 0.132, 0.16 x 10/12 x 1.2 = 0.16; SMM = 1 - (1 - CPR)^(1/12) and the cash flows computed in decimal at 60 digits. Loan B7 (annuity, 50,000 at 9%, six months to 2024-07-31, seasoned beyond a_ramp): I = 0.055, k (I - x0) = 4.5 and CPR = (0.02 + 0.28 logistic(4.5)) x Season(month); the May and June factors 1.2 and 1.1 lift it above c_max, so the clamp is at 1, not at c_max. Property: in each trial PM1 parameters inside the contract constraints, the margin and the observed rate of each currency are drawn from the seeded generator; a parallel shock of 0, and of -0, must give every projected month of every loan (CPR, SMM and the six amounts) identical to BASE. Negative control: the same comparison detects a 1bp shock in every trial. Kept out because the contract leaves them open: burnout (b = 0), several tenors per currency and penalties (both need the remaining term in years), and shocked rates below zero (the post-shock floor).
